index.t168: A row is one instrument for one algorithm, and the marker colour shows which. Four instruments are traded by both algorithms and therefore appear in the list twice: XAUUSD, EURJPY, NZDUSD and USTEC.
index.t169: The average RR column together with the win rate reveals the mechanics of a source. Gold takes 6.67 per unit of risk at a 20% win rate — rarely, but in large amounts; the euro-yen is the opposite, 0.40 at a 76% win rate — often and in small amounts. Both designs are profitable but behave in opposite ways, and they fall into drawdown at different times.
index.t170: Note the drawdowns: the individual drawdown of a source does not add up into the portfolio one — the sum of all eighteen would be 130%, while the portfolio drew down 16.3%.
index.t171: Gold brings in the most: +259% from Algorithm 2 and +46% from Algorithm 1, together a third of the entire result. The dependence on it is softened by the fact that these are two different algorithms with different entry rules — not one bet doubled in size.
index.t172: The outer periods are shorter than the rest — the history begins in August 2021 and ends in August 2026. Counted as full years from the start, the spread is even: +172%, +203%, +203%, +187%, +205% — all five are profitable, and none accounts for more than a quarter of the total. The result does not rest on a single lucky year.
index.t173: The average win is 1.73% of the deposit against an average loss of 0.85% — a ratio of 2.05 at a share of profitable trades of 42.7%.
index.t175: This is the strategy’s debut on the platform. The historical calculation exists; live statistics are only beginning — and accumulating them is the main task right now. The goal for the coming year: to build up a full body of live trading statistics that can be presented not as words but as an export from the platform.
index.t176: That is why the fee is below market at the moment. The usual rate for copy trading is 25–30% of profit; a strategy without a public track record has no right to ask for that much. As statistics accumulate the rate will rise — but only for new subscribers: the terms of an existing subscription do not change once it has been set up. Whoever joins at the start stays on the starting terms.
index.t177: Work on the system continues. The set of instruments is not frozen: each new one goes through the same selection — a stability check across the two halves of history, a test against randomness, an assessment of execution costs. Whatever fails is not added, even if it looks profitable. A third algorithm with independent entry logic is in development.
index.t178:
Every expansion of the set has reduced the portfolio’s
  drawdown rather than increasing it: instruments are chosen so that they lose
  in different periods. That is the point of adding new ones — not so much a rise
  in return as a smoothing of the dips.
index.t180:
Everything set out here is a calculation on historical data, not the result of live
  trading. History describes the past; the future may turn out differently, and the actual
  drawdown may exceed 41%. Live statistics are only starting to accumulate —
  and they are what should be treated as the main evidence once they exist.
index.t181:
The algorithms are independent in their results, but not entirely independent
  in their design. A market regime in which both draw down simultaneously is theoretically
  possible. In five years of history this has not happened: they were simultaneously
  negative four times in 61 months, and on each occasion the losses were insignificant.
index.t182:
Copying is executed at current market prices, so a subscriber’s result
  will differ from the strategy’s. On accounts smaller than $1,000 the
  divergence is noticeably larger because of rounding in position size.
index.t184: Calculations on 2021–2026 history. Not investment advice.
